decisions.location: raw_data.csv, lines 338-339 (and PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: brown-iannuzzi2017_1.html, Discussion, line 440)
decisions.reason: Two projects in Boyce et al. (2023) replicated Brown-Iannuzzi et al. (2017, DOI 10.1177/0956797616674999): brown-iannuzzi2017_1 (Supplement Study 3 with Study 1 images, N = 43, m1 = 3.42 [2.98, 3.86] vs. m2 = 3.98 [3.62, 4.34], same_dir = yes, replicated_instructor_code = 1, replicated_report_code = 1) and brown-iannuzzi2017_2 (Study 3, N = 29, F(1, 56) = 16.72, same_dir = yes, replicated_instructor_code = 1, replicated_report_code = 1). In addition, the attached primary project report for brown-iannuzzi2017_1 (line 440) explicitly concludes: 'We are able to fully replicate the original study finding... we consider our replication to be successful and to support the theory of Brown-Iannuzzi et al. (2016).' Both shipped and blind (target 121) needed primary verification because blind lacked an outcome quote; primary evidence confirms the overall replication outcome is 'successful'.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt With 25 participants for the final analysis (2 excluded for attention check failure), a paired t-test was ran. The result was significant with p=.001, suggesting that participants were more likely to favor truth responses for black targets rather than white targets. This finding replicates the Lloyd et al. (2016) study 1c result. Commentary I believe that this study was accurate replication of Lloyd et al. (2016) study 1c findings. With the help of the original researchers, I was able to acquire materials and procedures necessary for a successful replication.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: lloyd2017.html, Discussion, line 622 (and raw_data.csv, line 323)
decisions.reason: The primary project report for lloyd2017 (replicating Study 1c of Lloyd et al., 2017, DOI 10.1177/0956797617705399) reports a statistically significant effect in the same direction as the original study (t(24) = 3.6168, p = .001) and explicitly concludes that the finding replicates Study 1c and is a successful replication. Likewise, raw_data.csv (line 323) records same_dir = yes, replicated_instructor_code = 1, and replicated_report_code = 1. Primary evidence confirms the shipped and blind (target 106) outcome 'successful'.

decisions.reason: For petersen2017 (replicating Study 1 of Petersen, 2017, DOI 10.1177/0956797617728270), the individual student report was not included in the bundle (replication_report_included = no), so raw_data.csv is the authoritative primary record in the source text. Compared to the original statistically significant effect (N = 600, b = .34, 95% CI [.10, .61]), the replication (N = 224) found a non-significant coefficient with a large standard error (b = 0.3661, SE = 0.2423), and both independent coders rated replication success as 0 on the [0, 1] scale (replicated_instructor_code = 0, replicated_report_code = 0, adjudicated_replication_code = NA). This confirms the shipped and blind (target 148) outcome 'failed'.
